reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - CMV clearance observed in 25/36 treated patients (69.4% clearance rate) with CMV PCR/culture conversion from positive to negative. This demonstrates that ganciclovir successfully engaged viral DNA polymerase and inhibited viral replication. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The intended mechanism (DNA polymerase inhibition leading to viral replication inhibition) was clearly demonstrated by the conversion of CMV PCR/culture from positive to negative in responding patients. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint was met with 69.4% CMV clearance rate, which represents successful clinical translation of the antiviral mechanism. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported, but 76% compliance rate suggests the treatment was generally tolerable in the target population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm study without a control group, but the 69.4% clearance rate is clinically meaningful for CMV reactivation treatment. High rates of laboratory abnormalities (86.1% ALT elevation, 86.1% hemoglobin decrease) represent expected toxicity profile for ganciclovir but did not prevent efficacy.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm design without control group limits ability to definitively attribute efficacy to treatment versus natural history, though 69.4% clearance rate exceeds typical spontaneous resolution rates
